projects.title: Credit-Eligibility Platform
projects.summary: Ingests financial statements from PDF, spreadsheets, bank files and accounting exports, then scores companies for short-term credit eligibility.
projects.description: The Intelligent Financial Assistant, a .NET 8 finance platform for short-term credit eligibility. Client companies are onboarded and approved by an admin team after review, then submit about three years of historical statements plus ongoing annual, monthly and bank statements (PDF, CSV, XLSX). ETL pipelines normalise balance sheets and income statements and compute metrics such as liquidity and debt-to-equity, while RabbitMQ workers run the processing with real-time status over SignalR. Blazor portals give admins and clients grid, pivot and chart reporting. I designed and built it end to end over more than three years: architecture, database, APIs, Blazor front ends and workers. It ships as six deployables: the Admin app, the Client app, the Admin API, the Client API, a PDF-processing service and a custom-ingestion background worker. It is in production and still evolving.
challenges: Turning fragmented PDF table output into balance sheets and income statements, including multi-page statements
Normalising many input shapes (PDF, templated spreadsheets, bank CSVs, accounting exports) into one model
Making reloads safe when files are re-uploaded or jobs are retried
Giving users live progress for long-running processing
outcomes: Heuristic PDF pipeline: weighted keyword scoring, note-page rejection and a page-stitching state machine
Common extract/transform/load contract across six ingestion paths, with raw-to-validated staging tables
Transactional bulk loading with SqlBulkCopy and temp-table MERGE upserts
Accounting-ratio engine (liquidity, solvency, coverage, turnover) on decimal arithmetic
RabbitMQ-driven workers with real-time status to the browser over SignalR
Blazor admin and client portals with Syncfusion grids, pivot tables and charts, Excel export and a step-by-step monthly upload wizard

Admin side: a 46-page Blazor Server admin app on a separate Admin API with its own JWT and CORS settings, admin user management with Admin and Operations roles, a staged client and borrower approval workflow, master data management and a daily onboarding-progress monitor
APIs for client onboarding, admin approval and statement uploads, including re-upload of an already processed month
187 versioned database migrations managed with DbUp
Six deployables: Admin app, Client app, Admin API, Client API, PDF service and custom background worker
projects.role: Full-stack engineer and principal engineer on the platform: architecture, database design, APIs, ETL and workers, and the Blazor front ends.

projects.title: Multi-Sport Data ETL Services
projects.summary: Per-sport .NET 8 ETL services that load provider feeds into SQL Server in bulk; the American football service adds a SQL outbox relay publishing events to RabbitMQ.
projects.description: A family of ETL services, one per sport, that pull schedules, box scores, projections and reference data from external providers (SportsDataIO for American football and basketball, Roanuz for football and cricket) and load them into per-sport SQL Server databases. The American football solution is the most complete: a clean-architecture layout (domain, application use cases, data access, hosted workers), raw provider payloads kept in MongoDB, and an outbox relay that publishes calculation events to the multi-tenant fantasy platform.
challenges: Loading large weekly datasets repeatedly without duplicates or partial failures
Surviving unauthorized and transient provider API failures without losing a whole run
Publishing events exactly once from several instances without distributed transactions
Reusing one pattern across four sports and two providers
outcomes: Hosted worker services calling single-purpose use cases (reference-data sync, box scores by week, player projections by week, headshot sync) on a schedule
Bulk upserts through staging tables and MERGE, with a lookback window for incremental sync and per-match transaction boundaries
Item-level fault tolerance: a failing match or call is logged and skipped while the rest of the run continues
Outbox written in the same transaction as the game data; a hosted publisher claims batches with READPAST/UPDLOCK, retries with exponential backoff and jitter, and resets stuck locks
Typed shared event contracts consumed through EasyNetQ AutoSubscriber by the fantasy platform
Relational schema for competitions, tournaments, timeframes, teams, players, schedules, scores, quarters and scoring plays, with versioned migrations
Unit and integration-style data-access and API-client tests, and pipelines publishing the worker deployables
Player image pipeline that validates, resizes and publishes photos to blob storage
projects.role: Lead backend engineer and solution architect on the American football platform (schema, clean-architecture refactor, use cases, outbox, testing); built the football, cricket and basketball ETL services on the same patterns.
projects.diagramAlt: Architecture: provider feed to ingestion workers, use cases and data access into SQL Server with an outbox table, then an outbox publisher to RabbitMQ and typed consumers

projects.title: Textile ERP
projects.summary: An internal ERP for a textile unit (2018 to 2021): I worked on eight modules, built a custom fine-grained permission engine, wrote a metadata-driven setup framework, and sped up a daily management report. Most modules were still in progress when I left.
projects.description: An ASP.NET MVC and Web API system for a textile unit within a group of several garments units, replacing paper and spreadsheet tracking. The codebase has 548 entities and 159 controllers. I worked on the Inventory, Yarn Inventory (including yarn dyeing), Knitting, Production (grey fabric), Wash, CDA (Chemicals, Dyes and Auxiliaries store), Supply Chain (import LC, PI, purchase order) and Booking Analysis modules, most of which were still in progress when I left. I designed and implemented a custom fine-grained role-based access control engine (menu and security rules, with per-user and per-group permissions at screen and action level), with ASP.NET Identity and OWIN cookie sign-in for the web app and custom JWT bearer authentication for the API. I also wrote the Common Interface framework, in which each setup screen's fields, grids, lookups and SQL are stored as database rows and rendered by one generic API and view, and which the audit and compliance system I built also reuses, optimised a daily management report, and gathered requirements directly from factory teams.
challenges: Letting different people and groups see and change only their own screens and actions across dozens of modules
Keeping stock transactions (receive, QC, issue, return, transfer) consistent across a long production chain
A management report that took about 10 minutes every morning
Avoiding a new controller, view and script for every setup table
outcomes: Custom RBAC engine: menu and security rules mapped to groups and users, with per-menu select, insert, update and delete permissions plus feature and report rules, instead of attribute-based roles
Hybrid authentication: ASP.NET Identity with OWIN cookies for the MVC app and a custom JWT bearer scheme (authorization attribute and custom principal) for the Web API

Permission model details: security rules grouped under user groups, with per-menu select, insert, update and delete flags, feature and report rules, and a per-user, per-application and per-company menu tree served by a stored procedure; the Web API's authorization attribute is applied across 138 controllers

Module work across stock and production flows: yarn receive, issue, return and transfer; knitting; grey-fabric production and QC; wash batches and requisitions; CDA (Chemicals, Dyes and Auxiliaries) floor and QC requisitions and rack/bin allocation; import LC, PI and purchase-order screens; booking analysis

Common Interface: a metadata-driven setup-page framework (screen, fields, grids, lookups and SQL stored as configuration rows, served by one generic API and view), so new setup pages need no new code; it is also reused by the audit and compliance system I built
Daily management report cut from about 10 minutes to 1 to 2 minutes through SQL rewrites, indexing and an API
projects.role: Senior engineer and unofficial team lead: wrote the project architecture from scratch, made the framework and technology decisions, worked on eight modules, built the permission engine and Common Interface, and mentored four senior engineers without a formal title.

projects.title: Support Monitor (Admin & Risk Platform)
projects.summary: A role-restricted support and risk admin platform: live match monitoring, withdrawal approvals, KYC and payment screens, panic alerts and push notifications. I designed and built it end to end.
projects.description: An internal admin platform for a support and risk team, built at Smart ABG. It has an ASP.NET Core API and an MVC admin UI. The API issues JWTs with user and role claims and restricts every admin endpoint to a SupportAdmin role. The UI signs users in with a cookie session built from the token's claims. A RabbitMQ consumer pushes live match events to the browser over SignalR. Admins can approve or reject withdrawal requests, check KYC and payment status, review panic-alert history and send Firebase push notifications. I designed and built the database scripts, project architecture, back-end API and front end.
challenges: Giving support staff live visibility of matches without direct access to production data
Restricting a money-related admin surface to one trusted role, end to end (API and UI)
Keeping an audit trail for withdrawal decisions
outcomes: Layered API (Api, Core, Infrastructure, integration and migration projects) with Dapper data access and FluentValidation
JWT issued by the API with user and role claims; every admin controller requires the SupportAdmin role
MVC admin UI with cookie sign-in from JWT claims, plus login, registration and password-reset flows
Live match monitor: RabbitMQ consumer to SignalR hubs for match events, scores and panic alerts
Withdrawal approval screens, with status-change audit columns (who and when) added by a migration
KYC status, user payments, panic history and Firebase push-notification screens
Injection-hardening of filter parameters in the data services; versioned database scripts with DbUp
projects.role: Designed and built the platform end to end: database scripts, project architecture, back-end API and front end.

projects.title: Fantasy Sports Platform (in progress)
projects.summary: Multi-tenant fantasy sports back end: daily contest creation, and leaderboard workers that consume match events idempotently. American football is implemented; the platform did not reach full release.
projects.description: A white-label fantasy sports platform on .NET 8 and SQL Server. A contest-creation worker creates American football tournaments daily. A leaderboard worker subscribes to match status events published by the sports data services over RabbitMQ, applies them with a per-match checkpoint, updates points in one transaction, and polls for matches whose events were missed. Each white-label operator has its own database, resolved per request. The leaderboard side was only partly finished: American football is implemented end to end, other sports are stubbed, and prize calculation is a placeholder.
challenges: Keeping leaderboards correct when events arrive twice, late or not at all
Isolating each white-label operator's data while sharing one API
Structuring the contest and leaderboard logic so more sports can be added
outcomes: Daily scheduled worker that creates American football tournaments, with run-now override and retry policy

Leaderboard worker subscribes (EasyNetQ AutoSubscribe) to match-updated and match-final events published by the sports data services and starts leaderboard processing; a checkpoint on the source-updated timestamp skips duplicate or older events
Polling hosted service that finds matches with pending updates and reprocesses them when events were missed
One database transaction per match: player points, team totals and tournament-match final state are updated together
Database-per-operator tenancy resolved per request from the broker context and bound to the caller through a JWT claim
Per-sport processing entry points in place (football, cricket, basketball, baseball, hockey) pending implementation
Unit and integration-style data-access tests for contest, team and settings commands and queries
projects.role: Sole author: designed the multi-tenant, database-per-operator model and the event-driven leaderboard flow, and built the APIs, workers and data-access layer.
projects.diagramAlt: Architecture: RabbitMQ match events to the leaderboard worker, checkpoint and a single transaction updating the operator database, with a polling fallback, a daily contest worker and the API

projects.title: Brokerage Back-Office & Billing
projects.summary: Automates trade ingestion, position roll-up, brokerage calculation and monthly invoicing for a futures and options introducing broker.
projects.description: A back-office system that loads trade files and clearer data, rolls trades into positions, calculates per-lot brokerage and generates monthly invoices as PDF and CSV for email delivery. I led the port of a legacy .NET Framework billing system to a layered .NET 5/6 application, and later built a sister product for OTC equity order and fill capture.
challenges: De-duplicating trades across files that identify the same trade differently
Resolving a broker code from any of several alias columns
Keeping web requests fast while long jobs (file load, invoicing, sending) run elsewhere
Isolating data between broker legal entities
outcomes: Worker pipeline: file load, roll-up, brokerage, validation, invoicing and sending, driven by job rows
Brokerage rules covering per-lot, per-trade, percentage and split-party rates, plus OTC trades
Invoice generation per client and currency with PDF and CSV output
Idempotent clearer-file ingestion over SFTP
Broker-entity multi-tenancy through JWT claims
OTC equity module with an 8-step deposit-form wizard that generates compliance PDFs
projects.role: Designed the pipeline and led the legacy port, working with a small team under a product owner.

projects.title: Clean Architecture Reference Platform
projects.summary: A .NET 8 reference implementation with compiler-enforced layer boundaries, proposed to engineering leadership for a multi-tenant SaaS product.
projects.description: While maintaining APIs for an EHS SaaS platform, I designed a working reference architecture to show how a legacy monolith could move to a modular one. It covers authentication, per-request tenant resolution, a reusable list-view query pipeline and architecture tests that fail the build on layer violations, and I presented it with an executive brief and developer guide.
challenges: Proving a strict architecture is practical inside an existing legacy codebase
Keeping legacy password and token formats working with new endpoints
Building one safe, reusable pipeline for filtered, sorted, paged lists
Resolving each request's tenant database without leaking credentials
outcomes: Eight architecture tests enforcing layer dependencies in CI
List-view pipeline with 16 filter operators, global and per-field search and row-level authorization
Per-request tenant connection resolution with encrypted credentials
Six sign-in paths: password, one-time code, session token, impersonation and reset
Hybrid data access: EF Core for writes with audit snapshots, Dapper for reads
projects.role: Designed and built the reference platform and wrote the executive brief and developer guide.
